Operator context prefers a single consolidated DATE column over three integer parts, but the column-level action model here maps one bronze column to one silver target and cannot merge year, month, and day into a derived column; time_hour already carries the consolidated UTC date-and-hour instant, so year/month/day are retained as integers pending a later modeling-layer consolidation.

Per operator context naming convention, measures are renamed with their unit as a suffix (temperature_fahrenheit, dew_point_fahrenheit, humidity_percent, wind_direction_degrees, wind_speed_mph, wind_gust_mph, precipitation_inches, pressure_millibars, visibility_miles) and abbreviated names are spelled out.

purpose: This table provides cleaned, hourly ASOS weather observations for the three NYC airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) covering January through June 2013, intended to feed downstream joins against flight records keyed by origin station and time.
usage: Join on origin_code and time_hour (a UTC timestamp) to align with flight-level data; be aware that wind_gust, pressure, and wind_direction_degrees carry nulls (74.6%, 11.5%, and 1.7% respectively) that must be explicitly handled, typically by filtering or coalescing, rather than assumed to be zero.
limitations: year, month, day, and hour remain as separate integer columns rather than a single consolidated DATE because the cleanup model maps one bronze column to one silver target; consumers who need a calendar date should derive it from these parts or from time_hour, which already encodes the full UTC instant. wind_gust is retained despite being 74.6% null, and pressure and wind_direction_degrees retain nontrivial null rates (11.5% and 1.7%) that were not imputed.
